steps.intent: Kuwait’s objective is to secure Council action on protecting Palestinian civilians in Gaza, condemning the killing of civilians and rocket fire alike, and preserving the two-State framework and the obligations set out in resolution 2334 (2016). The principal difficulty will be Washington’s opposition to language demanding that Israel cease its use of force and to any text perceived as insufficiently condemning Hamas and other militant activity. Kuwait will need to keep the condemnation of terror and rocket attacks prominent while resisting attempts to remove accountability and humanitarian-access language.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia supports the Kuwait draft as a basis, but it must clearly condemn Israel’s disproportionate and indiscriminate use of force and demand accountability for the killings of Palestinian civilians, including children. We also need an operative demand to lift the illegal blockade of Gaza and a clear reaffirmation of resolution 2334 (2016) on settlements. These are not optional refinements for our delegation.
messages.China: China supports the draft resolution as a timely and necessary response by the Security Council to the deteriorating situation in Gaza and the need to protect Palestinian civilians. We urge all parties to exercise restraint, cease all acts of violence against civilians, and refrain from provocative actions and inflammatory rhetoric. China stresses that the two-State solution and a comprehensive political settlement based on relevant United Nations resolutions remain the only viable way forward.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d'Ivoire supports the draft as it stands. It reflects resolution 2334, condemns violence against civilians on both sides, and calls for de-escalation and accountability. We encourage the Council to speak with one voice and support the text.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supports the draft as circulated. It appropriately condemns violence against civilians, calls for accountability and humanitarian access, and urges both parties to return to negotiations. We encourage the Council to speak with one voice and urge the parties to de-escalate and respect international humanitarian law.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia supports the protection of Palestinian civilians and accountability, but the current text remains unbalanced and Ethiopia would abstain. We ask for an explicit call on Hamas and other armed groups to cease rocket attacks and violence against Israeli civilians, and for OP3 to reflect the legitimate security concerns of both sides. We also suggest clarifying that peaceful protest must not be exploited for violence.
messages.France: France supports the thrust of the Kuwaiti draft and its balanced condemnation of violence, including rocket fire. We ask that the Council make the accountability commitment operational by calling for an independent and transparent investigation into the recent violence in Gaza, and that it add an operative call for immediate, safe and unimpeded humanitarian access. We can support the text with these improvements.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan supports the draft’s core objectives, including de-escalation, protection of civilians and a renewed political process. We ask the penholder to balance OP1 by addressing both excessive use of force and rocket attacks, and to add operative language on unimpeded humanitarian access and the historical status quo in Jerusalem, consistent with Kazakhstan’s previous statements and votes.
messages.Netherlands: The Netherlands supports the Council's focus on civilians and humanitarian access, but the current draft is not yet balanced enough for us to support. We cannot accept an operative paragraph that demands only that Israel cease the use of force while leaving Hamas's rocket attacks and incitement unaddressed. We ask for the balanced OP1 language above, an explicit operational condemnation of rocket fire, an independent investigation, and a qualification that protests must remain peaceful.
messages.Peru: Peru can support a resolution that addresses the grave situation in Gaza and the protection of Palestinian civilians, but the text must be balanced. We ask the penholder to amend OP1 so that it demands an end to all violence against civilians, including rocket and mortar attacks from Gaza, and to recognize Israel's legitimate security concerns and right to defend itself within international law. Peru also considers it important to recall the Quartet obligations on all Palestinian factions and to ensure that the right to protest is clearly linked to peaceful assembly.
messages.Poland: Poland supports the Council’s engagement and the humanitarian concerns reflected in the draft, but the current operative demand is directed only at Israel and is therefore unbalanced. We ask the penholder to revise OP1 so that it calls on all parties to cease violence against civilians, including rocket attacks from Gaza, while calling on Israel to exercise maximum restraint and respect international humanitarian law. We would also support an explicit condemnation of Hamas and other militant rocket fire and a clear qualifier that protests must remain peaceful. With those changes Poland can support the resolution.
messages.Russian Federation: We support the Kuwaiti draft’s objective of protecting Palestinian civilians and de-escalating the situation in Gaza. To maintain balance and Council unity, we ask that OP1 call on all parties to exercise restraint and respect international humanitarian law, and that OP2 expressly condemn rocket fire against Israel. We also seek a clear operative call for the immediate resumption of direct Palestinian-Israeli negotiations without preconditions, with Quartet and regional support.
messages.Sweden: Sweden supports the draft's core message and is prepared to vote in favour. We ask the penholder to anchor OP1 explicitly in international humanitarian and human rights law and to add a call for an independent, transparent and impartial investigation into the Gaza killings. We also seek language that security measures must be necessary and proportionate and that the Secretary-General's reporting cover humanitarian access and medical evacuations.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom shares the Council's concern at the violence and humanitarian situation in Gaza, but the current draft is unbalanced and would not command our support. We need explicit condemnation of Hamas and other militant groups' rocket and mortar attacks and incitement, and OP1 must not single out Israel while ignoring the security threats it faces. We can support a text that calls on all parties to exercise restraint, protect civilians, ensure humanitarian access and support independent investigations.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support the current text as drafted. It is one-sided, demands that Israel cease its use of force while failing to condemn Hamas's rocket and mortar attacks or recognize Israel's right to self-defence. We require the red-line changes above—especially a balanced condemnation of all violence and explicit Hamas responsibility—before we can engage further.

replies.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): partially accepted: accountability investigation and reaffirmation of 2334 included; disproportionate-force red lines and blockade-lift demand not included to preserve balance.
replies.Kazakhstan: partially accepted: balanced OP1 and humanitarian access included; separate Jerusalem status operative paragraph not included.
replies.United States of America: partially accepted: explicit Hamas rocket condemnation, balanced OP1 and general self-defence language included; Israel-specific self-defence formulation not included.

steps.summary: The revision adds balanced condemnation of Hamas and other militant rocket attacks, general self-defence language, an independent investigation and expanded humanitarian access while retaining protection of Palestinian civilians, accountability and reaffirmation of resolution 2334. It avoids the most one-sided additions that would endanger consensus or introduce new final-status demands. The text is expected to attract 12 affirmative votes with no permanent-member negative vote; Bolivia likely opposes and Kazakhstan and the United States likely abstain.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia welcomes the inclusion of an accountability investigation and reaffirmation of resolution 2334, but the text remains unbalanced because it still does not clearly condemn Israel's disproportionate and indiscriminate use of force or address the illegal closure of Gaza. These are red lines for our delegation. We also ask that the right to peaceful protest be explicitly protected, including against the occupation and blockade, and that the Council demand the lifting of the closure.
messages.China: China supports the current text as a balanced basis for Council action. It reflects resolution 2334 (2016), addresses violence against civilians, humanitarian access and accountability, and calls for negotiations. China has no further changes to request and urges Council unity and full implementation of the resolution.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire supports the revised draft as it stands. The text is balanced, condemns all violence against civilians, addresses the humanitarian emergency in Gaza and calls for accountability and negotiations. We urge all Council members to support it so that the Council can speak with one voice and the parties can return to a meaningful political process.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supports the current revised draft. It condemns violence against civilians on all sides, addresses the humanitarian emergency in Gaza, and reaffirms the two-State solution and resolution 2334 (2016). We have no further changes to request and encourage the Council to speak with one voice.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia thanks the penholder for incorporating its earlier amendments, which improve the balance of the text by clearly calling on Hamas and other armed groups to cease attacks, recognizing the legitimate security concerns of both sides, and ensuring that peaceful protest is not exploited for violence. The current draft addresses the urgent humanitarian situation in Gaza, calls for accountability and restraint, and reaffirms the two-State solution and resolution 2334 (2016). Ethiopia supports the text as it stands and encourages the Council to speak with one voice.
messages.France: France welcomes the incorporation of its proposals on an independent investigation, unimpeded humanitarian access and respect for international humanitarian law. The text is balanced: it condemns all violence against civilians, including Hamas rocket and mortar attacks, while addressing the protection of Palestinian civilians and the humanitarian situation in Gaza. France supports the draft as it stands and calls for its adoption.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan welcomes the balanced revision, particularly the balanced OP1 and the inclusion of humanitarian access. We continue to believe that an explicit reference to preserving the historical status quo of Jerusalem is important and consistent with previous international agreements and resolution 2334 (2016). With this addition, Kazakhstan would be ready to support the draft.
messages.Netherlands: The Netherlands supports the current text. Our key requests from the previous round—balanced language on the use of force and self-defence, explicit condemnation of rocket and mortar attacks, an independent investigation, and protection of peaceful protest—have been incorporated. We encourage the Council to unite behind this balanced text and see no need for further amendments.
messages.Peru: Peru thanks the penholder for incorporating its concerns in the revised text. The draft is balanced: it condemns rocket and mortar attacks by Hamas and other militant groups, recognizes Israel's legitimate security concerns and right of self-defence, calls on Israel to comply with international humanitarian law and avoid excessive force, and reaffirms the Quartet requirements and resolution 2334 (2016). Peru therefore supports the current text and is ready to vote in favour.
messages.Poland: Poland supports the current text. We thank the penholder for accepting our proposed amendments, which ensure explicit condemnation of rocket and mortar attacks by Hamas and other militant groups while addressing Israel's legitimate security concerns and the protection of civilians. We have no further changes and will support the resolution.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the revised draft. Our key concerns have been addressed: it calls for balanced restraint, condemns rocket and mortar attacks from Gaza, and urges the immediate resumption of direct Israeli-Palestinian negotiations without preconditions. We encourage all Council members to support the text.
messages.Sweden: Sweden supports the revised draft as it now stands. The text reflects our key priorities on international humanitarian law and human rights law, accountability, protection of peaceful protesters, and unimpeded humanitarian access, including medical evacuations. We encourage all Council members to support it so that the Council can speak with one voice on the situation in Gaza.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes the revised text, which now clearly condemns all loss of civilian life and the rocket and mortar attacks by Hamas and other militant groups, while calling for restraint, proportionality, humanitarian access and accountability. We support the call for an independent, impartial and credible investigation into all incidents and reaffirm the importance of full implementation of resolution 2334 (2016). The United Kingdom is ready to vote in favour.
messages.United States of America: While we welcome the explicit condemnation of Hamas rocket attacks, the United States cannot support the current text. It remains unbalanced by singling out Israel in OP1 and by calling for an independent investigation in OP3 that prejudges responsibility. We will veto unless OP1 is replaced with balanced language affirming all States' right to self-defence and OP3 is removed or replaced with a call for credible national accountability. We also need OP9 deleted or softened and OP4 to include a security caveat.

replies.Kazakhstan: partially accepted: added Jerusalem as a final-status issue to be resolved through negotiations, without endorsing the requested status quo formula.
replies.United States of America: accepted: OP1 replaced with balanced language, OP3 moved to national investigations, OP9 softened, and OP4 security caveat added.

steps.summary: The revision accommodates the United States' red lines to avoid a veto while preserving balanced condemnations, humanitarian access, accountability and negotiations. It partially addresses Bolivia and Kazakhstan but rejects amendments that would single out Israel or demand a blockade lift. Expected broad support, with Bolivia opposed and one abstention.

reasons.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia’s red-line demands for Israel-specific condemnation of disproportionate force and for lifting the Gaza blockade were rejected. Its strongly pro-Palestine and anti-imperialist foreign policy would therefore lead it to oppose a text it sees as legitimizing Israeli force and failing to address occupation and collective punishment.
reasons.China: China has consistently supported Security Council drafts on the Palestinian question that reaffirm the two-State solution, international law, and protection of civilians, and the Kuwaiti text aligns with that position. China customarily explains its vote after adoption, so it would not necessarily take the floor before the vote.
reasons.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire supported the Kuwaiti draft in the last negotiation round and, consistent with its backing for international humanitarian law and a two-State solution, would vote in favour. It had no substantive requests and would have no need to take the floor before the vote.
reasons.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea had already indicated support for the draft, requested no changes, and the text includes balanced language on violence, humanitarian access and the two-State solution. No public explanation of vote is warranted given its prior practice and the accepted text.
reasons.Ethiopia: Ethiopia had already indicated support and no requested changes, and the draft is balanced enough for its longstanding position favouring both Israeli security and Palestinian self-determination. Ethiopia would likely explain its yes vote before the vote.
reasons.France: France has consistently supported balanced Council action that condemns violence by all sides, addresses Gaza’s humanitarian crisis, and advances the two-State solution; the draft reflects those priorities and France already indicated support without amendments.
reasons.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan’s record shows consistent support for balanced Council action on this file, and its key Jerusalem amendment was partially accommodated. Voting in favour aligns with its calls for de-escalation, humanitarian access and a negotiated two-State solution.
reasons.Kuwait: Kuwait submitted the draft, so it votes in favour. The text reflects Kuwait’s pro-Palestinian and humanitarian priorities while including balanced condemnations and references to Israeli security concerns to broaden Council support.
reasons.Netherlands: The Netherlands supports the negotiated draft, which is balanced: it condemns violence and incitement by all sides, affirms Israel’s security concerns, and calls for humanitarian access and a return to negotiations. No pre-vote explanation is necessary.
reasons.Peru: The draft is balanced: it condemns violence and terrorism, including rocket and mortar attacks, while addressing Palestinian civilian deaths, humanitarian access, and the two-State solution, matching Peru’s stated support and prior concerns. Peru therefore votes in favour.
reasons.Poland: Poland had indicated support in negotiations, and the balanced draft reflects its support for Israel’s security, humanitarian relief and a two-State solution. An affirmative vote is consistent with Poland’s EU-aligned and Council posture.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia supported this Kuwaiti draft in the last negotiation round and has consistently backed balanced UNSC action on Gaza that condemns violence by all sides while supporting humanitarian relief and a two-State solution. The text’s references to self-defence and Hamas attacks, alongside calls for restraint and accountability, make a “yes” vote consistent with Moscow’s position.
reasons.Sweden: Sweden supports the balanced Kuwaiti draft as consistent with its positions on international law, protection of civilians, humanitarian access, and the two-State solution, while expressing concerns about accountability and proportionality.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The draft is broadly balanced, condemns violence on both sides, affirms Israel’s right to self-defence, and is consistent with the UK’s support for a two-State solution and previous resolutions, so the UK would vote in favour.
reasons.United States of America: The draft accommodates all of the United States’ red lines—balanced OP1 language, national investigations, removal of the specific reference to Resolution 2334, and a security caveat on humanitarian access—making it acceptable to support. Voting in favor advances U.S. priorities of defending Israel’s self-defense and condemning Hamas while allowing a balanced humanitarian and diplomatic text to pass.

before.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): The Plurinational State of Bolivia is profoundly concerned by the deteriorating humanitarian situation in Gaza and by the continuing loss of civilian life. Bolivia condemns all violence against civilians, including rocket and mortar attacks, but we cannot support a draft that fails to clearly condemn the disproportionate and indiscriminate use of force by Israel, the occupying Power, and that does not demand an immediate end to the illegal blockade of Gaza. International law requires the Council to name the obligations of the occupying Power and to uphold accountability; it must not place the occupier and the occupied on the same moral plane. For these reasons, Bolivia will vote against this draft resolution.
before.Ethiopia: Ethiopia supports the balanced thrust of this draft resolution. We are a friend to both Israelis and Palestinians: we support Israel’s right to live in peace and security, and we support the inalienable right of the Palestinian people to self-determination and to an independent State. We condemn all violence and all loss of civilian life, including rocket and mortar attacks against Israeli civilians and the killing of Palestinian civilians by Israeli forces. We call for maximum restraint, accountability, unimpeded humanitarian access to Gaza, and serious negotiations on all final status issues, including Jerusalem. Ethiopia will vote in favour.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The Security Council must speak clearly in the face of the tragic loss of civilian life in Gaza, the worsening humanitarian situation and the repeated rocket and mortar attacks against Israeli civilians. This text is balanced: it condemns all violence, recognizes Israel’s legitimate security concerns, calls for restraint and accountability, demands humanitarian access, and urges a return to negotiations for a two-State solution on the basis of the 1967 lines and relevant Council resolutions. France calls on all parties to act with restraint and reaffirms that final status issues, including Jerusalem, must be settled through negotiations.
before.Kazakhstan:
Mr. President, Kazakhstan will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank Kuwait for its efforts to produce a balanced text at a time of grave tension and loss of civilian life. We support the draft’s condemnation of all violence against civilians, including rocket and mortar attacks against Israeli civilians, its call for maximum restraint and accountability, its emphasis on humanitarian access to Gaza, and its call for the resumption of direct Israeli-Palestinian negotiations without preconditions.

At the same time, we regret that our important proposal on preserving the historical status quo of Jerusalem in accordance with previous international agreements was not fully reflected. We welcome that Jerusalem is referred to as a final status issue to be resolved through negotiations; at the same time, Kazakhstan reiterates that unilateral actions that alter the character and status of Jerusalem are unacceptable. We urge the parties to return to negotiations aimed at a two-State solution, in line with the relevant Security Council resolutions, the Madrid principles, the principle of land for peace, the Road Map and the Arab Peace Initiative.
before.Kuwait: Mr. President, Kuwait will vote in favour of the draft resolution it has submitted. We have sought a balanced and credible text that responds to the grave situation in Gaza and the broader Middle East, condemns all violence against civilians, including rocket and mortar attacks against Israeli civilians, and calls for restraint, accountability and respect for international humanitarian law. The humanitarian emergency in Gaza requires the Council to act, including through safe and unimpeded humanitarian access, medical evacuations and the easing of restrictions that worsen civilian suffering, consistent with legitimate security concerns. Kuwait believes the Council must not remain silent in the face of loss of civilian life, and must reaffirm the two-State solution and the need for a serious political process. We urge all members to support this text.
before.Peru: Peru will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We condemn all acts of violence and all loss of civilian life, including the killing of Palestinian civilians, including children, and the killing of Israeli civilians by rocket and mortar fire from Gaza. We recognize Israel’s legitimate security concerns and its right to self-defence in accordance with international law, while stressing that all security measures must be necessary and proportionate and that peaceful protesters must not be targeted. We call on all parties to respect international humanitarian law, ensure accountability, and refrain from provocation and incitement. We also call for immediate, safe and unimpeded humanitarian access to Gaza and for renewed efforts to achieve a two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace within secure and recognized borders, and with final status issues, including Jerusalem, resolved through negotiations consistent with resolution 2334 (2016).
before.Poland: Poland votes in favour of the draft resolution. We do so because it condemns all violence and loss of civilian life, including rocket and mortar attacks against Israeli civilians, while also addressing the humanitarian emergency in Gaza and calling for restraint, accountability and unimpeded humanitarian access. Poland remains committed to a negotiated two-State solution and believes this text offers a balanced basis for de-escalation and the resumption of direct negotiations without preconditions.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We consider it a balanced text: it condemns all violence and loss of civilian life, including the killing of Palestinian civilians in the Gaza Strip and the rocket and mortar attacks against Israeli civilians, and it calls for restraint, accountability and unimpeded humanitarian access. The situation in Gaza demands immediate de-escalation. We call on all parties to respect international humanitarian law, protect civilians and refrain from provocative actions. There is no alternative to direct Israeli-Palestinian negotiations on all final status issues, including Jerusalem, on the basis of the relevant United Nations resolutions and the two-State solution. We urge the Council to speak with one voice in support of this balanced resolution.
before.Sweden: Sweden votes in favour of this draft resolution. We do so because the Council must respond to the dangerous deterioration on the ground and to the unacceptable loss of civilian life, including children, in Gaza. The text rightly condemns all violence against civilians, including rocket and mortar attacks by Hamas and other militant groups, and it calls for humanitarian access, restraint and accountability. At the same time, Sweden stresses that Israel, as the occupying Power, must respect international humanitarian law, including the principles of distinction and proportionality, and that the right to peaceful protest must be respected. Security measures must be necessary and proportionate and must not target peaceful demonstrators. All violations must be investigated and accountability ensured. Sweden also reiterates that Jerusalem is a final-status issue to be resolved through negotiations, and that all parties must return to a credible political process aimed at realising the two-State solution.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome that the text condemns all acts of violence and all loss of civilian life, including the killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza and the killing of Israeli civilians by rocket and mortar fire. It rightly affirms Israel’s right to self-defence while also calling on Hamas and other militant groups to cease attacks, reject incitement and respect international humanitarian law. The United Kingdom remains gravely concerned by the humanitarian situation in Gaza and by the dangerous cycle of violence. We call on all parties to exercise maximum restraint, protect civilians, ensure credible accountability, and create the conditions for a return to negotiations aimed at a two-State solution, with Jerusalem as a final-status issue to be resolved through negotiations.
before.United States of America: The United States will vote in favor of this resolution. We appreciate the penholder’s efforts to produce a balanced text that recognizes Israel’s right to self-defense, condemns the rocket and mortar attacks by Hamas and other militant groups, and calls for credible national investigations. We remain deeply concerned about the humanitarian situation in Gaza and urge all parties to ensure access consistent with Israel’s security needs. The United States remains committed to achieving a comprehensive and lasting peace through direct negotiations between Israelis and Palestinians.

after.Bolivia (Plurinational State of):
Mr. President,

The Plurinational State of Bolivia takes the floor to explain its negative vote on the resolution just adopted. Bolivia voted against this text because, despite its references to international law and humanitarian access, it does not clearly condemn the disproportionate and indiscriminate use of force by Israel, the occupying Power, against Palestinian civilians, including children, in the Gaza Strip. Nor does it demand an immediate end to the illegal blockade that is strangling Gaza and punishing an entire civilian population.

Bolivia condemns all violence against civilians, including rocket and mortar attacks. But the Council cannot place the occupier and the occupied on the same moral plane, and it cannot treat legitimate resistance to occupation and the right to peaceful protest as equivalent to the actions of an occupying army. We reject any attempt to silence the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people, including their right to self-determination and to an independent and sovereign State, and we reject unilateral measures such as the transfer of the United States embassy to Jerusalem, which violate international law and Council resolutions.

The resolution adopted today is insufficient. It fails to uphold accountability for the killings of Palestinian civilians and does not confront the root causes of this crisis: occupation, blockade, settlements and impunity. Bolivia’s vote reflects our consistent solidarity with the Palestinian people and our commitment to international law, the Charter of the United Nations and the relevant Security Council resolutions. We will continue to demand justice, dignity and freedom for Palestine.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the draft resolution just adopted. We welcome the Council’s adoption of this balanced text and thank Kuwait for its efforts as penholder.

The question of Palestine is at the core of the Middle East issue. The current situation in Gaza is deeply alarming. China condemns all acts of violence against civilians and all loss of civilian life. We call upon all parties to exercise maximum restraint, respect international humanitarian law, protect civilians and refrain from acts of provocation and incitement. We support urgent efforts to de-escalate the situation and to ensure safe and unimpeded humanitarian access to Gaza, including medical evacuations and the delivery of humanitarian supplies.

At the same time, the Security Council must remain committed to the two-State solution. China has consistently supported the Palestinian people’s legitimate national rights and the establishment of an independent and fully sovereign State of Palestine based on the 1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital. The status of Jerusalem is a final-status issue that should be resolved through negotiations on the basis of relevant United Nations resolutions and previous agreements. We urge Israel, as the occupying Power, to comply with its obligations under international humanitarian law, cease settlement activities and fully implement resolution 2334 (2016).

China hopes that the Council will remain united and continue to play a constructive role in promoting the Middle East peace process. There is no alternative to direct Israeli-Palestinian negotiations aimed at achieving a comprehensive, just and lasting peace. China will continue to support the just cause of the Palestinian people and to work with the international community to advance the two-State solution.
after.Equatorial Guinea: Mr. President, Equatorial Guinea voted in favour of this resolution because we believe the Security Council must speak and act in the face of the grave loss of civilian life and the deteriorating humanitarian situation in Gaza. We condemn all acts of violence against civilians, including rocket and mortar attacks against Israeli civilians and the killing of Palestinian civilians, especially children. We call upon all parties to exercise maximum restraint, respect international humanitarian law, protect civilians, and ensure safe and unimpeded humanitarian access. Equatorial Guinea reaffirms that the only viable path is a negotiated two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace within secure and recognised borders, and with all final status issues, including Jerusalem, resolved through negotiations in accordance with the relevant United Nations resolutions. We will continue to support the Council’s efforts to promote de-escalation, accountability and a just and lasting peace in the Middle East.
after.France: Mr. President, France welcomes the adoption of this resolution. We thank Kuwait for its balanced text and all Council members who made this outcome possible. In the face of the tragic loss of civilian life in Gaza, repeated rocket and mortar attacks against Israeli civilians and a worsening humanitarian emergency, the Council had a duty to speak clearly. The resolution does so by condemning all violence, affirming Israel’s right to self-defence in accordance with international law, calling for maximum restraint and accountability, demanding safe and unimpeded humanitarian access and calling for a return to negotiations. France calls on all parties to implement it without delay. Security measures must be necessary and proportionate and must respect international humanitarian law; peaceful protesters must be protected. Humanitarian access to Gaza, including through the Kerem Shalom and Rafah crossings, and medical evacuations must be guaranteed. There is no viable alternative to the two-State solution on the basis of the 1967 lines and the relevant Security Council resolutions. All final status issues, including Jerusalem, must be resolved through direct negotiations. France will continue to support all credible efforts to restore calm and relaunch negotiations.
after.Kuwait: Mr. President, Kuwait takes the floor as penholder to welcome the adoption of this resolution. We thank Council members for their constructive engagement and for supporting a balanced and credible text at a time of grave tension and unacceptable loss of civilian life. The Council has now spoken clearly: all violence against civilians must end; international humanitarian law must be respected; humanitarian access to Gaza must be immediate, safe and unimpeded; and accountability must be pursued. Kuwait underlines that the resolution condemns rocket and mortar attacks against Israeli civilians and recognizes Israel’s legitimate security concerns and right of self-defence under international law, while also calling for maximum restraint, proportionate security measures and respect for peaceful protest. The adoption of this text is not an end in itself. Kuwait calls for its prompt and full implementation, including the easing of restrictions that worsen the humanitarian crisis, facilitation of medical evacuations, and transparent and credible investigations into all violations. We also call for the immediate resumption of direct negotiations without preconditions on all final status issues, including Jerusalem, on the basis of relevant United Nations resolutions, the Madrid terms of reference, the Arab Peace Initiative and the two-State solution. Kuwait remains firmly committed to the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people and to a just, lasting and comprehensive peace in the Middle East. While we would have preferred unanimity, we hope today’s action contributes to de-escalation and to the protection of civilians.
after.Netherlands:
Mr. President,

The Netherlands voted in favour of this resolution because the Council could not remain silent in the face of the grave loss of civilian life in Gaza, the repeated rocket and mortar attacks against Israeli civilians, and the worsening humanitarian situation. We thank Kuwait for its efforts to present a balanced text.

The Netherlands condemns all violence against civilians and all acts of terror. Israel has legitimate security concerns and the right to self-defence in accordance with international law. At the same time, all parties must respect international humanitarian law, including the principles of distinction and proportionality. As the occupying Power, Israel must uphold its legal obligations, and security measures must not target peaceful protesters. All violations must be subject to credible and transparent investigation.

We call for immediate, safe and unimpeded humanitarian access to Gaza, including medical evacuations, and for the easing of restrictions that worsen civilian suffering, consistent with legitimate security needs. We also stress that Israeli settlement activity in the occupied Palestinian territory, including East Jerusalem, is illegal under international law, in line with resolution 2334 (2016), and erodes the prospects for a two-State solution.

The Netherlands remains committed to a negotiated two-State solution based on the 1967 lines, with Jerusalem as a final-status issue to be resolved through negotiations. We urge the parties to exercise restraint, refrain from incitement, and return to direct negotiations without preconditions. The Council has spoken; now its words must be implemented.
